title: The List from Ten Thousand Years Ago
next_chapter_hook: At the moment when the Turtle Shell Divine Artifact's light pointed north, Chen Ji faintly sensed the familiar aura sealed within his father's relic—the final clue he had buried with his own hands ten years ago.

text.content: Chen Ji stared at the rare battle intent in the Eye of Heavenly Way, his heart's alarm ringing loudly. This will that stood above all living beings had never placed anyone in its eyes, yet now it had revealed a flaw because of one of his schemes. He forced himself to remain calm, hands clasped behind his back, knuckles turning faintly white within his sleeves. "Since the senior admits this junior still has some use, perhaps you could be more generous—what other inside information about the Chess Player battle ten thousand years ago does this junior not know?"

The Eye of Heavenly Way fell silent for a moment, an elusive light flickering in those cold pupils. Then, a scroll of yellowed silk slowly emerged from the void, with seven names barely visible upon it, each accompanied by dense annotations and symbols. Chen Ji's pupils contracted slightly—was this the legendary list of Chess Players from ten thousand years ago?

Chen Ji's gaze swept quickly across the seven names on the list. The first name had been eroded by time, too blurred to distinguish clearly, only a "Chen" character faintly recognizable; the second name read "Cang Tianming"; the third, fourth... each name had left legends in the ancient texts of the cultivation world, yet no one had ever known what they had joined forces to oppose. When his gaze fell upon the final name, Chen Ji's breath caught abruptly—there, unmistakably, was a "Chen" character, with a small annotation beside it: Substitute.

dialogue.content: "Substitute—not an official name, but a 'Substitute Chess Player.' The voice of the Eye of Heavenly Way remained cold, yet carried an unnoticeable hint of amusement. "Ten thousand years ago, six Chess Players fell in that great battle; only Cang Tianming survived alone. And the bloodline flowing through you happens to share the same origin as that fallen First Chess Player."

text.content: Chen Ji suppressed the shock in his heart, his expression remaining as unruffled as ever. "Does the senior mean that this junior merely stumbled upon the leftovers of predecessors?" A faint smile curved his lips. "Whether substitute or official, being able to reach where I am today, I relied on myself. As for those six who fell..." He paused. "Who killed them?"

The Eye of Heavenly Way's gaze flickered slightly, as if examining every nuance of Chen Ji's emotional fluctuation. "Killed?" Its voice actually carried a诡异 smile. "Did you think Chess Players could be easily slain? Their falls were part of the plan from the beginning. Including the outcome of that great battle—it too was within my calculations."

A bone-deep chill suddenly washed over Chen Ji. Countless images flashed through his mind—the origin of the Tianji Record Fragment, the tragic ends of generations of prophets, and the various coincidences along his own path. These seemingly independent events now connected in his heart into a terrifyingly coherent chain. "Does the senior mean... that we Chess Players have been your pieces all along?"

dialogue.content: "Pieces? The Eye of Heavenly Way's voice suddenly carried a rare mockery. "You overestimate yourselves. The only true Chess Player is me. As for those seven names on the list... they are merely seven keys, used to open a certain door. Keys don't need their own will—they only need to be sharp enough."

text.content: Chen Ji's pupils contracted violently. Keys? Open what door? Just as he was about to press for answers, the Tianji Record Fragment began to tremble on its own, a familiar aura spreading from his chest. He下意识地将手探入袖中, touching the Turtle Shell Divine Artifact—a warm force instantly flooded his mind. This was his father's final relic, resonating with the list.

He discovered a line of extremely faint script at the edge of the list, almost integrated with the silk itself—"The door is at Kunlun, the keys belong to fate." What did this mean?

He decided to暂时按下不表, observing quietly. "The senior said keys don't need will—where are these seven keys now?" he continued, his voice steady enough to betray no波动.

text.content: Chen Ji suddenly laughed lightly, his gaze fixed directly on the core of the Eye of Heavenly Way. "The senior said there is only one Chess Player—you. Then this junior dares to ask: since you are so powerful, why bother arranging these seven keys? Beyond the true chess game, is there an existence even you cannot control?" The moment his words fell, the Turtle Shell Divine Artifact resonated strongly again, a faint light shooting from Chen Ji's chest, pointing precisely northward.

The Eye of Heavenly Way's gaze followed that faint light turning north, and an uncommon gravity flickered in the depths of its pupils. "What is that?" Its voice was no longer the lofty审视 but carried a few points of genuine wariness. Chen Ji's heart stirred—what existence could evoke such emotion from the Eye of Heavenly Way? He vaguely sensed the direction the Turtle Shell Divine Artifact pointed to, where some power sufficient to overturn cognition seemed sealed.

Chen Ji narrowed his eyes, his mind racing through his father's dying words. "Remember, no matter what happens, don't go north..." At the time, he thought his father meant the Kunlun Forbidden Grounds, but now it seemed that phrase held another meaning. North—what was there that could make even the Eye of Heavenly Way change color? He pressed this question to the bottom of his heart, deciding to first extract more intelligence from the Eye of Heavenly Way.

dialogue.content: "You don't need to know. The Eye of Heavenly Way's voice suddenly恢复了往常的冷漠. "That is not within your chess game, nor should it be touched by you. A substitute should have a substitute's觉悟—your task is to complete the Tianji Record's inheritance, not to追问 those matters unrelated to you. Having spoken, those cold pupils slowly closed, and the list too dissipated into the void.

However, in the instant his head lowered, the corner of his lips curved into an almost imperceptible arc. The more the Eye of Heavenly Way refused to speak, the more important the secret of the north must be—Chen Ji excelled at tearing open a gap in the most desperate circumstances.

text.content: Chen Ji straightened up, his gaze calmly meeting the Eye of Heavenly Way. "Since the senior says this junior is a substitute, this junior dares to ask—what if this junior refuses to complete the inheritance?" The Eye of Heavenly Way's pupils contracted sharply, an无形威压 like a mountain crashing down. Yet Chen Ji laughed, lighter than at any previous moment. "The senior is angered? This proves my existence is not dispensable to you."

The Eye of Heavenly Way gave no response, but Chen Ji clearly sensed that gaze becoming deeper. He knew he was dancing on the blade's edge—but this was precisely the game he excelled at. So what if he was a substitute? The falls of six Chess Players, Cang Tianming's忍耐, the war ten thousand years ago... these puzzle pieces were gradually taking shape in his mind, outlining a picture far more grand and dark than he had imagined.

Just then, the Turtle Shell Divine Artifact transmitted another gentle vibration. Chen Ji took the opportunity of adjusting his sleeve to grip the artifact in his palm, that warm force responding to a念头 in his heart. He closed his eyes,灵力缓缓注入神器, and a blurred image emerged in his mind—a remote mountain in the north, an ancient stone house covered by vines, and within it a wooden box thick with dust.

"That is... Chen Ji喃喃自语, his pupils suddenly dilating. The style of that stone house he knew too well—it was precisely where his father had lived in seclusion! Could the relic left by his father contain secrets even more important than the Tianji Record? He forcefully suppressed his excitement, face betraying nothing. The Eye of Heavenly Way still watched nearby—he could not reveal any flaw. So what if he was a substitute? The Chen family's fate had always been held by the Chen family themselves.

Chen Ji took a deep breath, raised his head, and stared directly into those cold pupils of the Eye of Heavenly Way. His voice was calm to the point of coldness: "The senior may rest assured, this junior knows his limits. This junior will remember the substitute's觉悟." Having spoken, he turned and left, his back决绝 yet elegant. The Eye of Heavenly Way did not阻止, only in those eternally cold eyes did a久违的战意再次浮现—it knew that the most restless piece on the chessboard had begun its own schemes.

After leaving the domain of the Eye of Heavenly Way, Chen Ji stood alone in the void, the Turtle Shell Divine Artifact gripped tightly in his hand. His thoughts surged like a tide—Chess Player list, substitute identity, heavenly fate locks and keys, father's relic... these seemingly independent clues were weaving into a net capable of tearing the heavens. And he, standing at the net's center, was about to become the fulcrum撬动一切. The northern stone house, father's secrets, and that blurred "Chen" character on the list—all answers pointed in the same direction.

Chen Ji slowly closed his eyes, pressing the Turtle Shell Divine Artifact against his chest. His father's dying words echoed once more in his ears: "Ji'er, the north... don't go... unless you have become strong enough." Now he finally understood—his father was not阻止ing him, but protecting him. What was sealed in that stone house might be not just the Chen family's secrets, but the true origin of that catastrophe ten thousand years ago. When he opened his eyes again, his gaze was as sharp as cold stars—he had already made his decision.
